subject: Learning Methods
title: Step Four: Review and Repeat
description: A quick, practical guide to Step Four: Review and Repeat.

hook.text: After filling your gaps and simplifying, try explaining the full concept again from scratch.

buildup.text: Each iteration of the Feynman cycle removes jargon, clarifies structure, and tightens your mental model.

discovery.text: Mastery means your explanation gets shorter, not longer. When you truly understand, you need fewer words.

twist.text: People expect mastery to feel complex. Instead it feels like clarity. If it still feels complicated, keep simplifying.

climax.text: Repeat the cycle until your explanation is clear, concise, and jargon-free. That is when understanding is complete.

punchline.text: Mastery is when it gets shorter, not longer.

quiz.question: How do you know you've achieved mastery using the Feynman technique?
options: Your explanation becomes shorter, clearer, and jargon-free
You can recite the textbook definition from memory
